items.followUp: Define volume/volume percent and write its formula.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the mass of solute in a specified volume of solution.
rubric.description: States that mass/volume percent gives the mass of solute in 100 mL of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the mass of solute and the 100 mL (or 100 cm³) of solution.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the mass of solute per volume of solution as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula: mass of solute ÷ volume of solution × 100.

modelAnswer: Mass/volume percent is the number of grams of solute dissolved in 100 mL of solution.
Mass/volume % = (mass of solute in grams ÷ volume of solution in mL) × 100.

items.followUp: Write any three postulates of Bohr’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy particular paths around the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits or shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the electrons’ fixed orbits or shells.

rubric.why: Each permitted orbit corresponds to a definite energy.
rubric.description: States that each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the fixed-energy idea.

rubric.why: An electron in a permitted stationary orbit does not continuously lose energy.
rubric.description: States that electrons do not radiate or lose energy while in a fixed orbit.

rubric.why: Electrons change orbits by absorbing or emitting energy.
rubric.description: Describes absorption for an upward transition and emission for a downward transition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing both transitions.

rubric.why: The energy exchanged is the difference between the energies of the two orbits.
rubric.description: Relates absorbed or emitted energy to the difference between orbit energies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this energy-difference relation.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain fixed circular paths called orbits or shells.
Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
An electron does not radiate or lose energy while it remains in a fixed orbit.
An electron absorbs energy to move to a higher orbit and emits energy when it moves to a lower orbit.
The energy absorbed or emitted equals the difference between the energies of the two orbits.

items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and covalent compounds, then state three properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: An ionic bond results from electron transfer and the attraction between the ions formed.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond as the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete definition.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds consist of positive and negative ions held together by ionic bonds.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic compound as a compound made of oppositely charged ions held together by ionic bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the ions and their bonding.

rubric.why: Strong attractions between ions require considerable energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points (or a high melting point).

rubric.why: Ions can move and carry charge when the compound is molten or in solution.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for conductivity with a correct condition.

rubric.why: Crystalline form, water solubility, and hardness with brittleness are characteristic properties of ionic compounds.
rubric.description: States one additional valid property of ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one such property.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by the transfer of electrons.
An ionic compound is a compound made up of positive and negative ions held together by ionic bonds.
Ionic compounds are usually crystalline solids with high melting and boiling points.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, because their ions can move freely.
Many ionic compounds are soluble in water and are hard but brittle.
